title: Unclassified assignment literal: benign public id controls
summary: 1 input holding public identifiers that sit next to the credential and look like it but are not secret.
rationale: Providers publish identifiers (account, key or client ids) beside their secrets. Reporting one is a false alarm, and redacting it removes information a reader legitimately needs.

expectation.rationale: Relabelled by docs/decisions/2026-09-30-accept-credential-named-and-typed-neighbour-redactions.md: was must-not-flag/T2 on polar-token (expected silence); is policy/T3 on generic-token with the value under clientSecret as the secret span, expected action redact. clientSecret is a credential-named object member. Polar documents the checkout client secret as safe to expose, but a redaction of it costs output fidelity only, so the generic-token redaction is accepted policy (security-first). It is not a polar-token credential, so polar-token stays silent on it. No polar-token provider-format claim is made.

externalRefs.note: Legacy benchmark issue the suite slice was written for.
